title: Contract on Generic Functions
concept: Contracts on generic functions express pre/postconditions that are checked for every concrete type instantiation.
why: Generic code without contracts is a black box. With contracts, the compiler verifies your generic function behaves correctly for ALL types.
tips: Contracts on generic functions are type-checked against the constraints
Use multiple simple ensures rather than complex expressions
The contract is monomorphized along with the function — zero cost for each concrete type
common_mistakes: Using operations in contracts that aren't guaranteed by the type constraint
Forgetting that generic contracts must work for ALL types satisfying the constraint
Writing contracts that reference concrete type details
